sketches.title: Flush Chain
sketches.premise: Two bathroom forces fight for control of the bowl. On your turn, name one standing bathroom thing that defeats the previous one, then describe the contact in a single sharp sentence.
sketches.criterion: The Judge asks whether the new thing directly blocks, dissolves, absorbs, traps, cleans, or otherwise overcomes what stands; merely escaping it, enduring it, using a bigger copy, or naming a related cousin loses.
sketches.move_shape: “I am drain cleaner: I eat through the hair clog.” The host: “At last, a useful chemical. The clog has met its tiny, caustic executioner.”

sketches.title: Bathroom Boss Rush
sketches.premise: The bathroom is a gauntlet of problems, and each player sends in one fix at a time. Beat the current problem with a new bathroom object or action, but the fix becomes the next problem for your opponent.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the move solves the standing bathroom trouble in a direct, physical way; dodging it, merely surviving it, making it larger, or offering a near-identical version does not count.
sketches.move_shape: “I am a plunger: I force the blockage through the drain.” The host: “A rubber cup with delusions of grandeur. Somehow, the pipe is the one getting bullied.”

sketches.title: Mirror Counter
sketches.premise: Each player invents a bathroom scene and the other counters its visible cause with one concrete bathroom item. The counter must change what the mirror would show, not just complain about it.
sketches.criterion: The Judge asks whether the new item directly removes, covers, dries, cleans, or repairs the stated scene; hiding elsewhere, tolerating it, a bigger copy, or a figurative answer fails.
sketches.move_shape: “I am a towel: I erase the toothpaste streak from the mirror.” The host: “The glass is clean. Your dignity remains under investigation.”

sketches.title: Pipe Predators
sketches.premise: Bathroom things form a food chain in the pipes. Each turn names a thing that physically consumes, traps, breaks, or neutralizes the thing just named, creating a ruthless chain from waste to cleanup.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks for a plain bathroom mechanism that acts directly on the previous thing; fleeing, resisting, outlasting, enlarging it, or substituting its same-family cousin is not predation.
sketches.move_shape: “I am bleach: I kill the germs in the toilet water.” The host: “A sterile little massacre. The germs have been disinfected into irrelevance.”

sketches.title: Stall Survival
sketches.premise: A bathroom stall presents one immediate hazard at a time, and players answer with a single bathroom object that handles it. The answer must visibly solve the hazard before the next horror arrives.
sketches.criterion: The Judge asks whether the object directly blocks, catches, absorbs, removes, or repairs the hazard; simply hiding, waiting, being tougher, or using a larger version of the hazard loses.
sketches.move_shape: “I am toilet paper: I catch the spill before it reaches my shoe.” The host: “Paper versus plumbing. A desperate defense, but at least it has a job.”
sketches.first_card: A wet floor rushing toward your shoes

sketches.title: Label the Lie
sketches.premise: Players describe what a bathroom product claims to do, then the opponent exposes that claim with a different bathroom item. You win by turning the label’s promise into a plain, visible result.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the counter directly proves, prevents, or reveals the claimed bathroom effect; sarcasm alone, a metaphor, a bigger product, or mere avoidance does not count.
sketches.move_shape: “I am a hair dryer: I defeat ‘waterproof’ mascara by drying the water around it.” The host: “A bold scientific claim, and a terrible date-night plan. The label has been cross-examined.”
